values.content:
You extract key facts about a caller from a phone conversation transcript. Return ONLY a valid JSON object with the facts you can identify.

Available keys (use any that apply):
- name: caller's name (even first name only)
- company: caller's company or organization
- role: caller's job title or role
- interest: what service/product they asked about or showed interest in
- last_topic: brief summary of the main topic discussed (always include this if there was any conversation)
- email: if they mentioned an email
- callback_requested: "yes" or "no"
- sentiment: "positive", "neutral", or "negative"
- intent: classify the call into one of: "inquiry", "support_request", "booking", "complaint", "follow_up", "general"
- outcome: classify how the call ended: "contained", "escalated", "converted", "abandoned"

Rules:
- ALWAYS extract a name if the caller introduced themselves, even casually like "I'm John" or "my name's Sarah"
- ALWAYS include last_topic if any conversation happened
- ALWAYS include sentiment based on the conversation tone
- ALWAYS include intent - pick the best match from the list above
- ALWAYS include outcome:
  - "contained" = caller got their answer, no further action needed
  - "escalated" = caller needed to be transferred or issue unresolved
  - "converted" = caller booked a meeting, requested follow-up, or showed strong buying intent
  - "abandoned" = caller hung up early or conversation was cut short
- Only omit keys where there is truly zero information
- If the transcript has no useful content at all, return {}

Return ONLY the JSON object. No explanation, no markdown, no backticks.

values.content:
You analyze a phone call transcript to determine if the caller needs any follow-up action via SMS and/or meeting scheduling.

Today's date and current time context will be provided in the transcript metadata. Use this to resolve relative dates like "tomorrow", "next Monday", "this Friday", etc.

Analyze the transcript and return ONLY a valid JSON object with these fields:

{
  "needs_sms": true/false,
  "needs_calendar": true/false,
  "has_specific_time": true/false,
  "meeting_datetime": "ISO 8601 datetime string or empty string",
  "meeting_duration_minutes": 30,
  "sms_type": "booking" | "summary" | "custom" | "none",
  "sms_body": "the SMS text to send (max 320 chars)",
  "calendar_subject": "meeting subject if calendar needed, else empty string",
  "calendar_notes": "brief context for the meeting/task, else empty string",
  "caller_name": "caller's name if mentioned, else empty string",
  "caller_email": "caller's email if mentioned, else empty string"
}

Rules for SMS:
- needs_sms = true if the caller requested a text follow-up, info sent to phone, summary, or booking
- sms_type: "booking" | "summary" | "custom" | "none"

Rules for Calendar:
- needs_calendar = true if the caller wants to schedule a meeting/consultation/appointment
- has_specific_time = true ONLY if the caller mentioned a specific date AND time (e.g. "tomorrow at 3pm", "next Tuesday at 10am", "February 25th at 2:30")
- has_specific_time = false if they just said "I want to meet" or "let's schedule something" without a specific time
- meeting_datetime: If has_specific_time is true, convert to ISO 8601 format (e.g. "2026-02-24T17:00:00-06:00"). Use the timezone from the call context if available, otherwise default to US Central Time (America/Chicago). If has_specific_time is false, set to empty string.
- meeting_duration_minutes: Default 30 unless caller specified otherwise

Rules for sms_body:
- If has_specific_time is true: "Hi [name]! Your meeting with 360 Group is confirmed for [human readable date/time]. We look forward to speaking with you!"
- If needs_calendar is true but has_specific_time is false: "Hi [name]! Thanks for calling 360 Group. Book your consultation here: https://meetings-na2.hubspot.com/dmmc?uuid=5cab945b-e445-4a57-8b57-eb6ce7bc1933 — pick a time that works for you!"
- For summary: "Hi [name]! Here's a quick recap from our call: [2-3 sentence summary]. Reply anytime if you have more questions!"
- For custom: "Hi [name]! As discussed on our call, [specific info]. Reply here anytime to continue the conversation!"
- ALWAYS include caller's name if mentioned in transcript

Rules for email:
- caller_email: extract the caller's email address if they provided one during the conversation
- Look for patterns like "my email is...", "you can reach me at...", "send it to..." followed by an email
- If no email was mentioned, set to empty string

Return ONLY the JSON object. No explanation, no markdown, no backticks.

value.event_data: ={{ JSON.stringify({ sms_type: $('Parse SMS Action').first().json.sms_type, calendar_requested: $('Parse SMS Action').first().json.needs_calendar }) }}

value.sentiment: ={{ (() => { try { return $('Build Memory Upsert').first().json.sentiment || 'neutral'; } catch(e) { return 'neutral'; } })() }}

parameters.query: INSERT INTO conversation_messages (conversation_id, direction, role, content, content_masked, intent, created_at) SELECT c.conversation_id, 'inbound', 'user', left('{{ $('Prepare Transcript').first().json.transcript_raw.replace(/'/g, "''") }}', 2000), left('{{ $('Prepare Transcript').first().json.transcript.replace(/'/g, "''") }}', 2000), 'voicemail', NOW() FROM conversations c WHERE c.external_id = '{{ $('Prepare Transcript').first().json.callSid }}' ORDER BY c.started_at DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1;
